messages:
maya: quick check-in — i want to float an idea about a smaller-surface refactor for the continuous batching scheduler. proposal: introduce a compact 'queue interchange' wire contract between admission and scheduler so we can swap scheduling backends without reshaping admission logic. tradeoffs?

jin: sounds promising. main worry is copy/serialize cost at hot path. if we add a marshal/unmarshal per enqueue we could regress p50.

kevin: +1 to an interchange contract, but maybe we keep it memory-resident objects only and expose a thin binary header for cross-thread handoff. avoid allocs.

olga: can we sketch the contract? do you mean a proto or just a serializable struct?

maya: proto for versioning, but minimal. think ~3 fields: queue_id, token_estimate, deadline_hint. proto sample:```proto
message QueuePacket {
  string queue_id = 1;
  uint32 token_estimate = 2;
  uint64 deadline_ns = 3;
}```

randall: proto gives safety for evolution but implies (de)serialize. what about an inlined shared struct with ABI version header so we can map it directly from shared mem? cheap, no copy.

jin: that shared-mem idea is nice for same-process shuffles. but for remote scheduler (dedicated mode) you'll need network-friendly format anyway. maybe two paths: fastpath (shared mem) + fallback (proto).

kevin: agree on dual-path. fastpath = direct struct + atomic enqueue. slowpath = proto over ipc. need clean interface: Admission.enqueue(packet) should take an opaque blob and a tag indicating path.

olga: we should also discuss semantic guarantees. what does admission promise? best-effort enqueue vs strong ordering? preemption?

maya: good point. proposal: admission guarantees "offer" semantics (non-blocking), and returns an outcome enum: ENQUEUED | REJECTED | STASHED. scheduler decides eviction/preempt. keep admission side deterministic and tiny.

randall: love keeping admission tiny. it reduces coupling. but where do headroom signals live? if scheduler sees pressure it should send a compact backpressure token to admission so admission stops offering heavy requests.

jin: backpressure channel should be push-based, not poll. scheduler -> admission: {queue_id, credit_delta}. lightweight, maybe a single atomic per queue.

kevin: we also need to account for per-tenant QoS. exchange should carry tenant hints for fairness. tiny header: tenant_id (u64) and cost_hint.

olga: telemetry: we must tag enqueue path and path type (fast/slow) so we can see how often we hit slowpath. otherwise perf regressions invisible.

maya: agreed. add a 1-byte path enum in header for telemetry. also log sample events for slowpath with stacktrace.

randall: corner case: kvcache eviction. scheduler may evict KV entries when it decides to preempt. need contract for multi-phase disposal. maybe scheduler returns a ReclaimIntent that admission actuator implements asynchronously.

jin: or treat kvcache eviction as separate subsystem with its own messages on reclaim bus. keep queue interchange free of KV semantics.

maya: leaning to separate bus to avoid bloating queue packet. we can add a best-effort refs count in packet for optimization but not required.

kevin: micro-bench ask: can someone prototype with in-process shared struct + atomic ring and measure token path cost? if < 200ns we ship.

olga: i'll spin up a tiny harness tomorrow. also, propose we keep the proto definition in repo under runtime/api so both private + hosted stacks can share.

maya: final open questions: 1) dual-path impl complexity vs maintenance cost, 2) backpressure granularity (per-queue vs global), 3) how to surface outcomes to higher-level routing policy.

randall: my two cents: implement fastpath first in a narrow area (same-host admission->scheduler), keep proto for cross-host. drive with telemetry.

jin: +1. add a feature-flagged rollout. will need oncall docs for diagnostic flags.

infra-bot: deploy: canary job queued: runtime/queue-interchange-harness (ci/42) — running.

maya: thanks all. i'll draft a short RFC follow-up capturing the contract, enums, and rollout plan. tagging @kevin @jin to help with perf tests and telemetry keys. :thumbsup:
